messages:
linh: noticed an alert from the snapshot-monitor: some DB snapshot objects show encryption=NONE in metadata even though uploader started with kmsKeyName. weird.
enc-ops-bot: alert: 5 snapshot objects missing kmsKeyName in gs://snapshots/prod/2026-04-01/ first_seen=1999999950
samir: hmm — did we do any multipart upload changes or switch proxy agents?
jessica: we deployed backup-agent v2.3.1 yesterday to improve multipart retries. rollout at 02:00 UTC.
matt_o: multipart uploads can sometimes strip metadata if the compose step doesn't carry metadata through. check the final compose object metadata.
linh: running quick check: gcloud storage objects describe gs://snapshots/prod/2026-04-01/snap-20260401-{1..5} --format=json | jq '.kmsKeyName, .metadata'
jessica: logs: agent uploaded parts with kmsKeyName present, final compose call returned 200 but response payload has no kmsKeyName. agent code uses storage.composeParts(..., preserveMetadata=true) — will inspect.
samir: could RBAC on KMS key ring deny rewrap after compose? if compose happens server-side without specifying kmsKeyName it ends up unencrypted?
oncall: check Cloud KMS cryptoKey IAM at 03:00-03:10 UTC for any Deny or removeBindings entries.
enc-ops-bot: suggested diagnostic commands: 1) list failed KMS operations: gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName=~".*encrypt|.*asymmetricEncrypt' --start-time="2026-04-01T03:00:00Z" --end-time="2026-04-01T03:10:00Z"
2) compare object ACLs and metadata before/after compose in audit logs.
jessica: grep in agent logs: "ComposeObject: parts=5 metadata_preserve=true final_request.kmsKeyName=null" — looks like our client removed kmsKeyName on the compose request.
linh: if client omitted kmsKeyName on compose, server will default to bucket-level default KMS if set; is default key configured?
matt_o: bucket had default KMS set to projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/kr-1/cryptoKeys/snap-key. that key exists. strange it isn't applied.
samir: check if compose is performed under a different service account which lacks project-wide default-encryption permission. the compose request identity matters for applying default KMS.
jessica: agent performs compose with serviceAccount:backup-composer@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com. I see an IAM change entry at 02:55 UTC removing roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter from group backup-team-temp. not the SA though.
oncall: quick mitigation: block further compose calls by throttling agent version or pin to v2.3.0. also add a conditional organization policy to deny creation of objects without kmsKeyName for snapshots prefix.
compliance: we might need to notify customers if snapshots are tenant-owned. please inventory affected tenant ids.
linh: listing affected objects and copying to quarantine bucket with preserved generation+md: gsutil cp -n -p gs://snapshots/prod/2026-04-01/snap-* gs://redwood-quarantine/200000/
jessica: adding hotfix: agent v2.3.2 will explicitly set kmsKeyName on compose requests. pushing canary now.
matt_o: forensic step: export Storage and KMS audit entries to BigQuery for the 03:00 window, will correlate principal and request IDs.
samir: long term: enforce bucket default KMS + org policy to prevent creation without kmsKeyName, update pre-deploy checklist to include compose metadata tests, and add unit tests for multipart compose to preserve encryption headers.
oncall: created incident: INC-2026-042; severity: medium.
compliance: please hold off customer notifications until we confirm scope. tag me when list is done.
linh: canary looks good, compose now includes kmsKeyName. starting re-ingest strategy discussion: rewrap vs reingest — rewrap requires key access to decrypt parts (not possible if parts were encrypted with missing key). reingest from DB backup source preferred.
jessica: we'll coordinate reingest for affected snapshots. owning remediation and postmortem.
samir: thanks team. I'll follow up with a draft postmortem and a proposed RBAC guardrail PR.
